verses.text: These are the last words of David. This is what David son of Jesse says, the man God lifted up high, the king chosen by the God of Jacob, the sweet song writer of Israel:
"The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me. His word was on my tongue.
The God of Israel spoke. The Rock of Israel said to me, 'A king who rules people fairly, who rules with respect for God,
is like the light of morning when the sun comes up, a morning without clouds. He is like the sunshine after rain that makes fresh grass grow from the ground.'

Isn't that how God has treated my family? He has made a covenant with me that lasts forever, arranged in every detail and sure. He will make my salvation complete and give me everything I long for. Won't he make it grow?
But wicked people are like thorns that are thrown away. No one can pick them up with bare hands.
Whoever touches them must use an iron tool or the shaft of a spear. They will be completely burned up in the fire where they lie."
These are the names of David's mighty warriors: Josheb-Basshebeth the Tahkemonite was chief of the officers. He was also called Adino the Eznite. He killed eight hundred men at one time.

Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodai the Ahohite. He was one of the three mighty warriors with David when they stood up to the Philistines who had gathered for battle. The other Israelite soldiers had pulled back,

but Eleazar stood his ground and struck down Philistines until his hand was so tired that it stuck to his sword. The LORD gave a great victory that day. The other soldiers came back to him only to take things from the dead.
Next to him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines had gathered at a place where there was a field full of lentils, and the Israelite soldiers ran away from them.
But Shammah stood in the middle of the field and defended it. He struck down the Philistines, and the LORD gave a great victory.
At harvest time, three of the thirty chief warriors went down to meet David at the cave of Adullam. A group of Philistines was camping in the Valley of Rephaim.
At that time David was in the fortress, and some Philistine soldiers were guarding Bethlehem.
David had a strong longing and said, "Oh, if only someone would bring me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!"

So the three mighty warriors broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as an offering to the LORD.

He said, "LORD, I could never drink this! It is like drinking the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it." So he would not drink it. These were some of the brave things the three mighty warriors did.
Abishai, the brother of Joab son of Zeruiah, was the leader of the Three. He once fought three hundred men with his spear and killed them, and he became as famous as the Three.
He was the most honoured of the Three and became their commander, but he was not one of the Three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did great things. He killed two of Moab's greatest warriors. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
And he killed a huge Egyptian who had a spear in his hand. Benaiah went against him with only a club. He grabbed the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
These were the brave things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he became as famous as the Three mighty warriors.
He was more honoured than the Thirty, but he was not one of the Three. David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
These were among the Thirty: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
Helez the Paltite, Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa,
Abiezer from Anathoth, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai from Netophah,
Heleb son of Baanah from Netophah, Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin,
Benaiah from Pirathon, Hiddai from the ravines of Gaash,
Abi-Albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam son of Ahithophel from Giloh,
Hezro from Carmel, Paarai the Arbite,
Igal son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai from Beeroth, who carried the armour of Joab son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
and Uriah the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
